title: A Long-term Study of the Safety and Effectiveness of RAP-219 in Adults With Focal Onset Seizures
official: An Open-label, Long‑term Study Evaluating RAP-219 in Adult Participants with Refractory Focal Onset Seizures
summary: Main objective: Part B and C: To evaluate the long-term safety and tolerability of RAP-219 in participants with refractory focal seizures
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Part B: Completed the Double-blind Treatment Period of the parent study (RAP-219-FOS-301 or -302) with acceptable tolerability, per the Investigator’s assessment
2. Part C: In the Investigator’s opinion, participant is and will likely continue to be able and willing to comply with all components of the study protocol, including administration of intact RAP-219 tablets by mouth, dosing and paper diary adherence and evaluations for the entire duration of the study.
3. Part B: Women of childbearing potential must agree to use of a highly effective or acceptable method of contraception from the first dose of study drug to the last study visit.
4. Part B: In the Investigator’s opinion, participant is and will likely continue to be able and willing to comply with all components of the study protocol, including administration of intact RAP-219 tablets by mouth, dosing and paper diary adherence as well as evaluations for the entire duration of the study.
5. Part C: Previously:  Has not participated in any previous clinical study of RAP-219
6. Part C: Aged 18 to 80 years at Visit 1
7. Part C: Diagnosis of focal epilepsy according to the ILAE classification of the epilepsies (Scheffer et al., 2017), and epileptic seizures (Beniczky et al., 2025) supported by: a. at least 1 brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT) scan and electroencephalogram (EEG) study, that may be normal but are compatible with focal epilepsy (ie, may be normal but do not suggest an alternative diagnosis to FS)
8. Part C: At least one FS in the Prospective Baseline Period as recorded in the paper seizure diary after Visit 1.
9. Part C: Women of childbearing potential must agree to use of a highly effective or acceptable method of contraception (as defined further in Section 6.2 of the protocol body) from the first dose of study drug to the last study visit.
10. Part C: Concomitant treatment with between 1 and 3 total ASM(s), inclusive, not including rescue or pro re nata (PRN) ASMs. Note: concomitant ASM dosing (dosage strength, frequency, and timing; formulation, and branded/generic drug product) must remain unchanged prior to Visit 1
Exclusion criteria:
1. Part B: Participation in any other interventional studies (aside from the parent study RAP-219-FOS-301 or -302) involving a study drug or device prior to Visit 1 or plans to participate for the duration of the study. Participation in observational studies is not exclusionary
2. Part B: Employment by or relation to an employee of the Sponsor, a Sponsor representative, or study site
3. Part C: For those participants with prior RAP-219 exposure, any Investigator concern that resumed RAP-219 dosing or study participation would place the participant at unacceptable risk, based on Investigator clinical assessment of this participant's prior RAP-219 exposure
4. Part C: For participants who previously enrolled in RAP-219-FOS-301 or -302, a history of frequent or severe RAP-219 dosing or other study conduct nonadherence during RAP-219-FOS-301 or -302.
5. Part C: Pregnant or breastfeeding, or intending to become pregnant during the course of the study
6. Part C: Epilepsy surgery prior to Visit 1
7. Part C: Current diagnosis of hepatic or renal failure, per Investigator
8. Part C: Treatment with any of the following concomitant medications: b. felbamate, unless dose regimen (dosage, frequency, and timing) remains unchanged for ≥12 months prior to Visit 1 with documented medical history indicating that LFTs and complete blood counts remained stable during that 12-month period c. vigabatrin, unless dose regimen (dosage, frequency, and timing) remains unchanged for ≥24 months prior to Visit 1 with documented medical history of normal visual fields for ≥12 months prior to Visit 1
9. Part C: Any of the following indicators of current or recent history of substance abuse: a. drug or alcohol dependency or abuse, per Investigator assessment b. positive drug screen, other than for cannabinoids and/or due to prescribed concomitant medications, at Visit 1
10. Part C: Participation or plans to participate in any other clinical study involving an investigational product or device prior to Visit 1. Observational studies are not exclusionary.
11. Part C: Known hypersensitivity to RAP-219 or any of its excipients
12. Part C: Employment by or relation to an employee of the Sponsor, a Sponsor representative, or study site
13. Part B: Pregnant or breastfeeding, or intending to become pregnant during the course of the study
14. Part B: Known hypersensitivity to RAP-219 or any of its excipients
